title: Offline-to-Online Quality Checker and Continuity Spec
author: Aisha Banerjee
body:
Overview

This document defines the Offline-to-Online Quality Checker (O2O-QC), a lightweight, production-facing continuity spec that ensures models promoted from offline evals remain within expected quality and resource envelopes once serving traffic begins. The O2O-QC bridges model-onboarding checklists, the eval harness, quantization profiles, and runtime guardrails to reduce regression windows and enable fast, safe rollouts.

Motivation

Despite strong offline metrics, models can exhibit operationally significant changes when exposed to live workloads (prompt distribution shift, embedding drift, KV-cache sensitivity, quantization degradation). O2O-QC establishes:

- A minimal, standardized set of signals to collect at promotion time and continuously afterward.
- Deterministic decision rules and thresholds for automated canary escalation and rollback.
- Integration hooks with the eval harness, rollout manager, and Alerting/Incidents.

Scope

Applies to all model promotions from "staging" -> "canary" -> "production" across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Focus areas include generation quality (semantic fidelity), latency/throughput regressions, token-cost changes, and quantization/kv-cache regressions. This spec intentionally excludes offline-only research metrics (e.g., FLOPs) unless they affect runtime behavior.

Key Concepts and Definitions

- Baseline snapshot: the canonical metric vector captured from the promoted model during offline certification (see "holistic-acceptance-matrix-for-model-promotion").
- Live delta: the rolling-window percentage change between baseline and production signal.
- Canary cohort: a controlled fraction of traffic (default 3%) used for early detection.

Signals to collect (minimum required)

1. Quality and correctness
- Prompt-level BLEU/ROUGE/MAUVE-like proxy where applicable (for structured outputs, use schema-validator failure rate).
- Rerank/semantic-similarity score distributions for retrieval-augmented tasks.

2. Distribution and embeddings
- Embedding population centroid drift (cosine distance) on automated sample of user requests.
- Token distribution shift (unigram/bigram KL divergence).

3. Runtime and economics
- P95 and P99 tail latency (ms).
- Avg tokens-per-request and tokens-per-second.
- Per-token compute cost estimate (normalized to baseline).

4. Cache sensitivity
- KV cache hit-rate and effective tokens saved.

Signal collection frequency and windows

- Baseline capture: Single pre-promotion window of 50k representative prompts (or 24h representative traffic in shadow).
- Live windows: 1m, 1h, 24h rolling aggregates. Canary decisions use 1h windows with 15m sub-windows for early abort heuristics.

Decision rules and thresholds

Table: Primary decision thresholds (defaults; teams may tighten per workload)

| Signal | Trigger condition (canary abort) | Escalation condition (require human review) | Rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Semantic proxy delta | >= 6% decrease in 1h window | 3%–6% decrease sustained over 24h | preserves user-facing correctness |
| Embedding centroid cosine drift | >= 0.12 (1h) | 0.08–0.12 sustained (24h) | retrieval recall risk |
| P99 latency | >= 2x baseline or >1200ms | 1.3x–2x sustained | user-latency SLO protection |
| Tokens-per-request | >= 25% increase (1h) | 10%–25% increase (24h) | cost blowout guardrail |
| KV-cache hit-rate drop | >= 15% absolute drop | 7%–15% sustained | quant/cache interplay |

Notes: Thresholds are tunable per-customer and per-model class. For latency, absolute ceiling overrides relative change.

Automated canary policy

1. Start canary at 3% traffic for 24 hours by default.
2. Evaluate 1-hour windows at 60-minute mark and 15-minute early-check sub-windows.
3. If any abort trigger fires, automatically scale canary down to 0 traffic and mark the rollout as "failed-canary". Generate an incident (severity S2) with attached artifacts.
4. If only escalation conditions fire (no abort), notify owners and hold rollout for manual review; do not expand canary.

Artifacts to capture when a trigger fires

- Canonical sample of 1k requests that contributed to the signal delta (anonymized/pseudonymized).
- Model input/output pairs, embeddings, and similarity scores.
- Perf traces (p95/p99), allocation telemetry, and kernel selection info if available.
- Baseline snapshot used for comparison and eval harness run-id.

Rollback and mitigation runbook (executed automatically or manually)

1. Automatic actions (triggered by abort):
   a. Stop routing to the canary model variant.
   b. Re-route to prior production model variant immediately.
   c. Create incident in PagerDuty with template "o2o-canary-abort" and attach artifacts.

2. Initial human triage (within 30 minutes):
   a. Owner reviews artifacts, validates anonymization, and reproduces failure with the eval harness in shadow mode.
   b. If failure is due to quantization profile or KV-cache mismatch, attach relevant quant profile and cache stats.

3. Targeted mitigations:
   a. Apply a temporary config that increases batching/limits sequence length or switches to higher-precision path.
   b. If semantic quality degraded, roll back permanently or escalate to research for hotfix.

4. Post-incident follow-up:
   a. Update the onboarding checklist entry that failed and add a dedicated regression test to the eval harness.
   b. Run a 7-day shadow run to assert stability before reattempting canary.

Integration points and examples

- Eval harness: Use eval run metadata keys: run_id, seed_set, quant_profile_id. The O2O controller fetches the baseline using run_id at promotion. Example shim to fetch baseline: 

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  "https://eval-harness.internal/v1/runs/{run_id}/snapshot"

- Rollout manager (canary config snippet):

{ "canary": { "traffic_fraction": 0.03, "monitoring_windows": ["15m","1h","24h"], "abort_criteria": ["semantic_proxy_delta","p99_latency"] } }

- Alert payload example (JSON):

{ "alert_type": "o2o_canary_abort", "model_id": "gptx-7b-q", "canary_fraction": "3%", "trigger": "semantic_proxy_delta", "details": "6.8% decrease in 1h window", "artifacts": ["s3://o2o-artifacts/2025-09-08/run-12345/sample-1000.json"] }

Operational guidance and ownership

- Primary owner: Applied ML (model-onboarding) team. Secondary owners: Serving Runtime and Platform SRE.
- PagerDuty routing: Severity S2 -> model-onboarding escalation; Severity S1 only for catastrophic regressions (widespread production failures).

SLOs and reporting

- Canary abort reaction time: initial triage within 30 minutes, mitigations started within 2 hours.
- Canary false-positive tolerance: <5% of canaries aborted due to transient noise per quarter.

Testing and verification matrix

- Add canonical tests to the eval harness for: adversarial prompt slices, token-inflation probes, and cache-stress scenarios.
- Label new onboarding bundles with quant_profile_id and cache_mode to ensure reproducibility.

Appendix A — Example prompts for stress probes

1. Token inflation probe: repeat patterns that trick autoregressive step-sizing.
2. Cache eviction probe: long-context prompts that simulate shifted KV-cache locality.
3. Retrieval drift probe: queries that exercise obscure domains to surface embedding shifts.

Appendix B — FAQ

Q: Who may relax thresholds for a high-value customer?
A: Only the platform SRE in coordination with model-onboarding and customer-security; document the exception and add compensating tests.

Q: How do we anonymize sample artifacts?
A: Use the internal pseudonymization script at /tools/anonymize-requests with the "--strip-pii" flag before upload.

- See "kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025" for quantization recovery steps.
